text.en:
(1) This Order may be cited as the National Retirement Scheme Order, 2023 and shall commence on 15th July 2023.

(2) The long title of this Order is "An Order to make provisions in relation to retirement and the establishment of the National Retirement Scheme payable to or in respect of employees and for matters connected therewith or incidental
This Order applies to all employees and members in an ordinary account or a SCP account.

(1) The Board may, with the consent of His Majesty the Sultan and Yang appoint such number of inspectors as it may consider necessary for carrying this Order into effect.

(2) In the course of an inspection, an inspector may at any reasonable time(a) enter any premises or place where he has reasonable cause to that a person is employed therein;

(b) examine, either alone or in the presence of any other person with to any matter under this Order or which he may reasonably require any person whom he has reasonable cause to believe to be or to have been an employee or an employer, and require every such person to be examined, and for the purposes of such examination may summon any such person to attend at the place and time specified in such summons; {c} put questions concerning employees to their employers or to any who may be in charge of them, or to the employees themselves, or to any other person whom he may consider desirable to question and the or employees or other person shall be legally bound to answer the questions truthfully to the best of his ability; {d} require any employer to produce before him all or any of the employed by him together with any contract of service, book of of salary, register and other document concerning employees of employment and to answer such questions relating thereto as he may proper to ask; {e} require any employer to produce for his inspection the audited of accounts of his undertaking and other records relating to the and to answer such questions relating thereto as he may think to ask; and {fJ make copies of any book, document or other records required to be produced under paragraph {d} or {e} and take possession of such book, or records when in his opinion(i) the copying thereof cannot reasonably be performed without taking possession;

(ii) the book, document or records may be tampered with unless possession is taken; or

(iii) the book, document or records may be required as evidence in any proceedings for an offence under this Order or in any for the recovery of any money due to the Scheme.

(3) If any personfa} wilfully delays an inspector in the exercise of any power under this section; {b} fails to -

(i) comply with the requisition of an inspector in pursuance of this section; or

(ii) produce any record, certificate, notice or document which he is required by or in pursuance of this section to produce; or {c) wilfully -

(i) withholds any information as to who are the employees of any or as to who is the employer of any employee; or

(ii) conceals or prevents or attempts to conceal or prevent a from appearing before or being examined by an that person is deemed to obstruct an inspector in the execution of his duties under this Order.

(4) Any person who obstructs an inspector is guilty of an offence. Power to examine persons

(1) Without prejudice to section 4(2), an inspector may, in the course of an examine orally any person supposed to be acquainted with the facts and circumstances of the case and shall reduce into writing any statement made by the person so examined.

(2) Such person shall be legally bound to answer the questions truthfully such case put to him by the inspector, but may refuse to answer any the answers to which would have a tendency to expose him to a criminal or to a penalty or forfeiture.

(3) A statement made by any person under this section shall be read over to him and shall, after correction if necessary, be signed by him.

(4) Any person who obstructs an inspector is guilty of an offence. Power to assess contributions based on information available

heading.en: to assess contributions based on information available

text.en:
( 1) An inspector may assess any contribution which is due by any based on any information available if the employer - fa) fails to keep or maintain any statement, particulars, register book or any record pertaining to each employee as required to be performed by him under this Order; or {b) fails or refuse to submit any statement, particulars, register book or record pertaining to each employee as required to be submitted by him this Order.

(2) The assessment made under subsection ( 1) shall be sufficient proof of the Board's claim for the summary recovery of any contribution under section 41. Powers of Managing Director to require information and application for search warrant

( 1) For the purposes of obtaining full information for ascertaining whether any person is liable to pay contributions under this Order, the Managing Director may, by notice in writing, require any personfa} to furnish the Managing Director within a time specified in the not being less than 30 days from the date of such notice, any or particulars specified in the notice; fb} to attend personally before the Managing Director or any person in that behalf by the Managing Director and produce for all books, accounts, records and other documents which the Managing Director or authorised officer deems necessary; or fc} to furnish the information or particulars in accordance with fa} and also to attend in accordance with paragraph fb}.

(2) Where a person is found guilty of an offence under subsection (4)fa}, the court before which the person is found guilty shall order such person to with the notice of the Managing Director under subsection ( 1) within 21 days from the date of the order of the court.

(3) Whenever it appears to any court, in written information on oath, and any enquiry it may think necessary, that there are reasonable grounds for that there are in particular premises any book, account, record or document the production of which has been required pursuant to

(1) and which has not been produced in compliance with that such court may issue a warrant authorising the Managing Director or any person named therein with or without assistance - fa} to search the premises and to break open and search any drawer, chest, trunk, box, package or other receptacle, whether or not, in the premises; and fb} to take possession of, or secure against interference, any book, record or other document that appears to be the book, account, or other document the production of which was so required.

(4) Any person who - fa} fails to comply with subsection (1); or (b} obstructs the Managing Director or any person named therein to in subsection (3), of an offence.

PART2

NATIONAL RETIREMENT SCHEME

(1) The Board shall establish and maintain a scheme to be known as the Retirement Scheme into which shall be paid all contributions collected this Order and out of which shall be met all payments to be made by the under this Order (including any costs and expenses incurred by the Board in establishing and maintaining the Scheme).

(2) If the Board is, at any time, unable to pay any sum which the Fund is to pay under this Order, the sum required to be paid shall be charged on and advanced to the Board from the Consolidated Fund and the Board shall, as soon as practicable, repay the sum advanced to the Government.

(1) Every employer of an employee shall pay to the Scheme monthly, in of each employee, contributions at the rates set out in Schedule 2: that the Board may, on such conditions as the Board may impose, an employer to pay contributions at other intervals not exceeding 6 months.

(2) Every employee shall pay to the Scheme monthly, in respect of contributions at the rate of 8.5 per cent of his wages. Payment of contributions

(1) Except where otherwise provided in this Order, the employer shall, in the first instance, be liable to pay both the contributions payable by himself and, on behalf of and to the exclusion of the employee, the contributions payable by that employee.

(2) Contributions payable by the employer for himself and on behalf of the under subsection ( 1) shall be paid in respect of the first and subsequent wages.

(3) For the purposes of this Order, contributions paid by an employer on of an employee are deemed to be contributions by the employee.

(4) Notwithstanding section 43, where an employer fails to pay any due within such period as may be prescribed, the employer shall, in such contribution, be liable to pay the rate of dividend which would have accrued on such contribution if the contribution had been paid at such rate and in accordance with such manner and calculations as the Board may

( 1) Subject to this section, the employer shall be entitled to recover from the employee the amount of any contribution payable on behalf of the employee.

(2) The amount of any contribution payable by the employer on behalf of the employee shall, notwithstanding any written law or any contract to the be so recoverable by means of deductions from the wages of the due from the employer to the employee and not otherwise.

(3) No deductions of any contribution shall be made - {a} except at the time wages are paid to the employee; and {b) other than the contribution in respect of the wages which are then being paid.

(4) Subject to such conditions as may be prescribed by the Board, where an employer has, by error not occasioned by the employer's negligence omitted to any contribution or part of any contribution payable by him on behalf of the employee, such contribution or part thereof may be deducted from the wages by such employee not later than 6 months from the date of payment of the wages in respect of which contribution or part thereof was omitted to be

(5) Any employer who contravenes subsection (2) or (3) is guilty of an
shall be payable on contributions to the Scheme respectively at such rate and in such manner and calculation as the Board may determine. Voluntary contributions by member or employer

Notwithstanding anything in this Order but subject to such conditions as the Board may impose - {a} any member or employer may at any time contribute voluntarily to the Scheme in such manner and at such rate as the Board may direct; {b) the Board shall credit every contribution received under {a} into member account in such manner as the Minister may and 15th. JUNE, 2023 (c} the Minister may give different directions in respect of different of members. Voluntary contributions by self-employed person

(1) Subject to any regulations made under section 53, any self-employed may at any time contribute voluntarily to the Scheme.

(2) Any self-employed person who chooses to pay voluntary contributions to the Scheme shall pay to the Scheme monthly, in respect of himself, at the rates set out in Schedule 2.

(3) The Board may, on such conditions as the Board may impose, any self-employed person or class of self-employed persons to pay under subsection (2) at other intervals not exceeding 3 months.

(4) Where any self-employed person has paid any voluntary contribution subsection (2), the Government shall match the person's contribution at the set out in Schedule 2.

(5) All contributions paid under this section shall be credited as provided section 16. Crediting of contributions into account

(1) Subject to subsection (2), the following accounts are to be maintained the Scheme - (a} a member account; and (b} a retirement account.

(2) The Board shall credit to the accounts specified in subsection (1) every paid into the Scheme for a member in such manner as the Minister may direct and the Minister may give different directions in respect of different of members.

(3) A member account referred to in subsection (l)(a} is an account for the crediting of every contribution paid into the Scheme by a or voluntary contribution by a self-employed person or employer, under this Order in such manner as the Minister may direct and the Minister may give directions in respect of different classes of members.

(4) A retirement account referred to in subsection (l)(b} is an account for the crediting of every contribution paid into the Scheme by an or self-employed person under this Order m such manner as the may direct. Transfer of amount from member account to another account

heading.en: of amount from member account to another account

text.en: The Board may, on the application of a member, transfer the whole or part of the amount standing to the credit of the member in the member account to the account in such manner as the Board may specify. Payment of cash grant by Government into Scheme

(1) The Board may accept any cash grant made by the Government for the of any person who qualifies for such grant under the Scheme and the Board shall credit the cash grant into the account of the person as the Minister may direct.

(2) Any cash grant paid into the Scheme under subsection (1) shall be disbursed in accordance with the conditions of the cash grant.

(3) Any cash grant paid into the Scheme under subsection (1) is deemed to be contributions for the purposes of this Order, but such cash grant or dividend shall not be withdrawn under any regulations made under section 53 the regulations expressly provide for the withdrawal of such cash grant.

(4) Notwithstanding anything in this Order, the Board shall be entitled to on behalf of the Government any cash grant paid into the Scheme for the of any person, together with any service charge which he is liable to pay the Government under the conditions of the cash grant, from any money standing to the credit of the person if he has - {a} obtained the cash grant by means of any false or misleading or any document that is false or misleading in any particular; or {b/ committed a breach of any of the conditions of the cash grant.

(5) Any money recovered by the Board from any person under

(4) shall be refunded forthwith to the Government.

(2) All moneys provided for under subsection (1) may be applied or by the Board for all or any of the purposes of the Scheme.

PART3 Authority for withdrawals from member account

(1) On an application for the withdrawal of the sum of money standing to the credit of a member by a person entitled thereto under section 20, the Board may authorise the payment to the applicant of such sum as the member is entitled to withdraw from the Scheme and any dividend calculated in accordance with 13 up to the date of the authorisation: that when{a} any contribution is due to be paid for a member in respect of any ending not later than the last day of the month next following the date on which the withdrawal of the sum of money standing to his credit in the Scheme is authorised; and {b} the contributions are not paid to the Scheme until after the date of the contributions may, in the discretion of the Board, be treated as if they had been included in the amount standing to the credit of the member at the date of of withdrawal and paid to the applicant accordingly.

(2) All applications for withdrawal shall be supported by such evidence as may be prescribed and by such further evidence as the Board may reasonably Authority for payment from retirement account

(2) Where a member has attained the minimum retirement age and has productivity, the amount of the monthly payment shall be determined on the formula set out by the Board and shall reflect, among other factors, the size of the member's retirement account balance at the time he attains the retirement age and in accordance with the following formula - x income replacement rate) x (years of contribution I productivity), means the average of salary applicable to an employee in with such manner and calculations as the Minister may replacement rate" means the percentage of an employee's premonthly income that he receives each month after retiring in with such manner and calculations as the Minister may

(3) Where a member has attained the minimum retirement age and has productivity and does not have sufficient amount in his retirement to finance a minimum monthly payment of at least $250, in accordance with the approved payment formula for the monthly payment prevailing at that time, such member shall receive such minimum monthly payment of at least $250 for a period of lifetime.

(4) Where a member has attained the minimum retirement age and has not reached productivity and does not have sufficient amount in his retirement to finance a minimum monthly payment of at least $250, in accordance with the approved payment formula for the monthly payment prevailing at that time, such member shall receive such minimum monthly payment of at least $250 until the amount in his retirement account is expended or for such as the Board may determine.

(5) The monthly payment may be adjusted periodically pursuant to made under section 53.

(6) Where a member is renouncing his citizenship of Brunei Darussalam or decides not to renew his Entry Permit issued under the Immigration Act 17) or his Entry Permit is cancelled and is about to leave Brunei such member is entitled to withdraw a lump sum of such expected as the Board may determine.

(7) Where a member dies before attaining the minimum retirement age, shall be paid to - (a} a widow or husband; (b} a widow or husband and children of the member; (c} children of the member; or

(d) parents, if such member has no widow or husband and children, a monthly derivative payment of an amount of 50 per cent of expected annuity or an amount of at least $400 collectively for a period of 15 years with effect from the date immediately following the death of the member: that the member has made contributions of at least 25 per cent of membership years of registration with the Board or has made active to the Scheme within 3 months before the month in which his death occurs.

(8) Where a member dies after attaining the minimum retirement age, shall be paid to - (a} a widow or husband; (b} a widow or husband and children of the member; (c} children of the member; or (d} parents, if such member has no widow or husband and children, a monthly derivative payment of at least $250 or an amount of 50 per cent of annuity to them collectively, or an amount as the Board may determine, with effect from the date immediately following the death of the member and up to the time the deceased member would have attained the age of 75 years, if living.

(9) Where a widow or husband in respect of whom a monthly derivative is granted under this section remarries or dies, such benefit shall be paid to the children to whom a monthly derivative payment is paid or payable under subsections (7) and (8).

(10) A child in respect of whom a monthly derivative payment is paid this section shall cease to be eligible for such benefit on such child the age of 21 years or on marriage below such age and such benefit shall be paid to other eligible beneficiaries under subsections (7) and (8). ( 11) If there is no eligible beneficiary - fa} the remaining monthly derivative payment; or {b} in the case of self-employed person, the remaining balance of the person's contributions, be paid to the administrator nominee in lump sum.

(12) For the purposes of this section, a husband in respect of whom a derivative benefit is granted shall be entitled to receive one derivative only. ( 13) In this section - means a person under 21 years of age and includesfa} a posthumous child; {b) a stepchild or illegitimate child born before the death of the and wholly or mainly dependent on him for support; and {c) an adopted child who is adopted in a manner recognised by any law before the death of the member and dependent on him for means, in the case of a deceased member who was a Muslim, all his legal wives living at the time of his death.

PART4

BY PERMANENT RESIDENTS HOLDING FOREIGN Application of this Part
This Part applies to every member who is a permanent resident holding a foreign citizenship. Authority for withdrawals from member account

(1) On an application for the withdrawal of the sum of money standing to the credit of a member by a person entitled thereto under section 24, the Board may authorise the payment to the applicant of such sum as the member is entitled to withdraw from the Scheme and any dividend calculated in accordance with up to the date of the authorisation: that when - (a} any contribution is due to be paid for a member in respect of any ending not later than the last day of the month next following the date on which the withdrawal of the sum of money standing to his credit in the Scheme is authorised; and

(b) the contributions are not paid to the Scheme until after the date of the contributions may, in the discretion of the Board, be treated as if they had been included in the amount standing to the credit of the member at the date of of withdrawal and paid to the applicant accordingly.

(2) All applications for withdrawal shall be supported by such evidence as may be prescribed and by such further evidence as the Board may reasonably Authority for payment from retirement account

(1) Where a member has attained the minimum retirement age and on by the member, there shall be paid to him monthly amount of at least $500 and such member shall receive such monthly payment until such is expended or for a period of 20 years.

(2) Where a member dies, there shall be paid to the administrator the balance of amount in the member's retirement account.

PARTS

ADMINISTRATOR NOMINEES Power to nominate administrator nominees

(1) A member who has attained the age of 18 years may nominate any as an administrator nominee to receive the amount standing to his credit and due to him at his death.

(2) A nomination may be made in favour of one person or a maximum of persons and such nomination shall be made in such form and manner as the may determine. Cessation of nominations

(1) A nomination shall cease to have effect(a} on the death of the administrator nominee or, where there is more than one administrator nominee, all the administrator nominees during the of the member; or

(b) by written notice of revocation. 15th. JUNE, 2023

(2) The cessation of nomination under subsection (l){bj shall not be revoked by any will or by any other means. Payment on death of member if there is nomination

heading.en: on death of member if there is nomination

text.en:
(1) Subject to subsection (2), where a member dies having nominated an nominee, the Board shall pay the amount standing to the credit of the deceased member according to the directions of the nominations.

(2) Where a Muslim member dies having nominated an administrator in accordance with this Order, the administrator nominee shall receive the amount standing to the credit of the deceased member as an executor and not beneficiary and shall distribute the amount in accordance with Hukum Syara'.

(3) In this section, "Hukum Syara, means the laws of Islam according to the Shafi'ee, Hanafi, Maliki or Hanbali sect of Ahlis Sunnah Waljamaah. Payment on death of member if there is no nomination

a member dies without having made any nomination, the Board pay any amount standing to the credit of the deceased member in with section 45.

PART6

OFFENCES, PENALTIES AND PROCEEDINGS

Any person who - fa} for any purpose connected with this Order -

(i) knowingly makes any false statement; or

(ii) produces or furnishes or causes or knowingly allows to be or furnished any document which he knows to be in a material particular; {bj fails to pay to the Scheme within such period as may be prescribed any amount which he is liable under this Order to pay in respect of or on of any employee in any month; fc} obstructs any officer or employee of the Board in the discharge of his functions as such; (dJ fails to comply with any regulations made under this Order; or (eJ fails to pay to the Board within such period as may be prescribed any amount which he is liable to pay under this Order, an offence. of information to unauthorised person

(1) Any person employed by the Board who, without lawful authority, or communicates to any person, otherwise than in the ordinary course of his duty or employment, any information acquired by him in the course of his duty or employment is guilty of an offence and liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or both.

(2) The Board may, on an application by a prospective employer who is whether or not to employ any person as an employee, give to the employer the following particulars of that person - (aJ the name of his employer or, if he has been in the employment of more than one employer, the name of all his employers during the past 3 and (bJ the period for which contributions were paid into the Scheme for that person by each of his employers.

(3) A prospective employer who wishes to obtain any of the particulars to in subsection (2) shall apply to the Board in such form and manner as the Board may determine and on payment of the prescribed fee.

(4) The Board may require an applicant under subsection (3) to furnish that he is considering whether to employ the person in respect of whom the application is made.

(5) No refund shall be made of any fee paid under subsection (3). Amount withdrawn not to be utilised for other purpose

heading.en: withdrawn not to be utilised for other purpose

text.en:
(1) An amount withdrawn by any member under this Order shall be the purpose for which the withdrawal was authorised.

(2) Where all or any part of the amount withdrawn under this Order is not the purpose for which the withdrawal was authorised, the member return all or such part of the amount which is not utilised to the Board 6 months from the date of the withdrawal.

(3) Any member who contravenes this section is guilty of an offence. by bodies corporate etc.

an offence against this Order or any regulations made thereunder by a body corporate, partnership, association or other body of persons is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or to be to any neglect on the part of, a director, manager, secretary or any of that body corporate, partnership, association or other body of or of any person purporting to act in any such capacity, he as well as the body corporate, partnership, association or other body of persons is guilty of that and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. for offences not otherwise provided for

heading.en: Penalty for offences not otherwise provided for

text.en:
(1) Any person who contravenes any prov1Slon of this Order or any made thereunder is guilty of an offence and if no penalty is expressly in this Order or the regulations made thereunder shall on conviction be not exceeding $3,000, and in the case of a subsequent offence, to a fine not exceeding $10,000 and the court before which the conviction is had shall, in addition to the fine, order him to pay the amount of any contribution together with any dividend due thereon certified by an officer appointed by the Board in that behalf to be due from that person at the date of the conviction and the may be recovered in accordance with the law for the time being in force the recovery of fines.

(2) Where an employer fails to comply with any order made under

(1), the court shall, on application by the Boardfa} issue a warrant for the levy of the amount by distress and sale of any property belonging to the employer; or (b} direct that in default of payment of the fine, the employer shall suffer imprisonment for a certain term. for prosecution
No court shall take cognisance of any offence under this Order or any made thereunder except with the sanction of the Public Prosecutor.

The Board may, with the concurrence of the Minister, compound any punishable under this Order or any regulations made thereunder by the payment of any sum of money as the Board thinks fit towards such being a sum not exceeding the amount of the maximum fine to which that person would have been liable if he had been convicted of the offence. for criminal proceedings
The provisions of this Order or any regulations made thereunder shall be prejudice to any other proceedings under any other written laws.

heading.en: of authorised officer to be evidence

text.en: In any legal proceedings, a copy of an entry in the accounts of the Scheme duly certified under the hand of such officer of the Board as it may authorise shall be prima facie evidence of such entry having been made and of the truth of the contents thereof.

in respect of any offence under the provisions of this Order or any regulations made thereunder may be conducted by an officer authorised in in that behalf by the Chairman of the Board. proceedings to recover contributions

(1) Notwithstanding the provisions of any other written laws, all payable under this Order may, without prejudice to any other remedy, be recoverable by the Board summarily as a civil debt.

(2) Proceedings for such summary recovery may be instituted by any authorised in writing in that behalf by the Board and that person may such proceedings.

(3) In subsection (1), "contribution" includes any dividend, service charge and penalty on any contribution charged by the Board under this Order or any made thereunder. of sums due to Scheme

Any sum due to the Scheme, including any sum required by the Board or by a court to be paid, repaid, refunded or transferred to any account for a member in respect of the moneys standing to the credit of the in the Scheme, may be sued for and recovered by the Board as if it were a debt due to the Government. 15th. PART7 Payment of service charge on contributions in arrears

heading.en: of service charge on contributions in arrears

text.en: l1) Where the amount of the contributions which an employer is liable to pay under this Order in respect of any month is not paid within such period as may be prescribed, the employer shall be liable to pay service charge on such for every day such amount remains unpaid commencing from the 16th day of the month succeeding the month in respect of which the amount is and the service charge shall be calculated at such rate and manner as the may determine. l2) The Board may, in any case in which it thinks fit, waive the payment of the whole or part of, or remit in whole or in part, any service charge due or paid under subsection ll). Refund of contributions paid in error

ll) When the Board is satisfied that any amount has been paid in error to the Scheme in respect of any person or as service charge under section 43, the Board may, subject to subsection l3), refund the amount so paid in error to the by whom it was paid or to any other person as the Board may determine: that if the refund of any amount paid in error is not claimed within 6 of the date on which it was paid or if the member in respect of whom it was paid has withdrawn it, the amount paid in error shall not be refunded but is to have been properly paid under the provisions of this Order as service or for the person in respect of whom it was paid. l2) If any amount is due to the Scheme from the person to whom refund of the amount paid in error would otherwise be made, the Board may retain the or any part of the amount paid in error and set it off against such amount as is due.

(3) No refund shall be made and no amount shall be set off under this section except with the consent of the Board who may require any person who claims to have paid any amount to the Scheme in error to make a written refund and to furnish such information as the Board may require to determine the amount so paid. Board to inform Probate Officer

Part 5, if the Board is satisfied that a member of the Scheme has died, it shall inform the Probate Officer who shall proceed forthwith to exercise his powers under section 13 of the Probate and Administration Act (Chapter 11). Preservation of secrecy

( 1) Except for the purpose of the performance of his duties or the exercise of his functions or when lawfully required to do so by any court or under the of any written law, no person who is or has been a member, an officer, an employee or an agent of the Board or a member of a committee of the Board shall disclose any information relating to the affairs of the Board or of any other which has been obtained by him in the performance of his duties or the his functions.

(2) Any person who contravenes subsection (1) is guilty of an offence and on conviction to a fine not exceeding $2,000, imprisonment for a term not exceeding 12 months or both.

heading.en: to obtain information and require production of documents

(1) Whenever a writ of seizure and sale has been issued in execution of a judgment against an employer and any movable or immovable property or other assets belonging to the employer has been seized or sold or otherwise realised in of the execution and, prior to the payment of the proceeds of the sale or other realisation to an execution creditor, notice has been given to the officer with the execution of the writ by the Board that any sum is due to the Scheme, no part of the proceeds shall be paid to an execution creditor unless and the court issuing the writ has ascertained and provided for the sum due to the Scheme at the date of the sale or other realisation.

(2) In the event of any interest in any place of employment being sold on the application of a secured creditor under any written law in force for the time and the Board giving to the officer charged with the conduct of the sale that a sum of money is due by the debtor to the Scheme, the proceeds of the sale shall not be paid to any creditor other than to the Government or a 15th. JUNE, 2023 secured creditor unless and until the court ordering the sale has ascertained and for the amount due to the Scheme at the date of the sale or unless the is satisfied that all sums due to the Scheme have been paid up to the date of sale. Joint and several liability by bodies corporate etc.

(1) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Order or any other laws, where any contribution remaining unpaid by a body corporate, association or body of persons(a} the directors or former directors of such body corporate;

(b) the partners or former partners of such partnership; or

(c) the members or office bearers of such association or body of as the case may be, during such period in which contributions were liable to be paid shall, together with the body corporate, partnership, association or body of liable to pay contributions, be jointly and severally liable for the due and payable to the Fund.

(2) In this section, "contribution" includes any dividend, service charge and penalties due to any contribution charged by the Board under this Order or any regulations made thereunder.
